summary: This note is a plot summary of the Office episode "The Carpet." Michael Scott becomes convinced that a prank on his office is a hate crime and terrorism and begins to distrust his employees. His mood reverses when he learns that his friend Todd Packer carried out the prank, which he finds hilarious. The episode closes with Jim cheered by seven voicemails from Pam.
one_line: Plot summary of the Office episode "The Carpet", in which Michael suspects an office prank is terrorism until Todd Packer is revealed as the culprit.
key_facts: Michael becomes convinced that what happened to his office is a hate crime and an act of terrorism.
Michael believes the act was perpetrated by someone in the office, causing him to lose faith in his employees, whom he considers his friends.
Michael tries talking to his former boss Ed Truck, played by Ken Howard.
Ed Truck tells Michael that he does not need to have his employees be his friends.
Michael's mood changes drastically when he finds out the prank was carried out by his obnoxious friend Todd Packer.
Todd Packer is played by David Koechner.
Michael finds the joke hilarious, and his faith in his friends is restored.
At the end of the day, Jim is cheered up when he finds that all seven of his voicemail messages were left by Pam throughout the day.
Jim is seen driving home as Pam's voicemails play as a voice-over, closing out the episode.
